result_text:
Template literals now count the same whatever they contain when units are compared for duplication. The tests I ran pass: `CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest` and the `JavaScript*` tests. I didn't run an end-to-end duplication report on two JavaScript functions.

- **Fix:** In `extraCleanContent` in `CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`, I added a step that turns `` `...` `` into ` `` `, right after the single-quote step. The text, including any `${...}`, is dropped, so two functions that differ only inside a template literal get the same cleaned body. Code outside the literal is untouched, so a difference there still keeps the units apart. The JavaScript extractor, and the other C-style extractors that extend this class, pick it up without further changes.
- **Test:** I added `cleanContentTemplateLiterals` to `CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest.java`. It checks that `` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` and `` `Hello beta ${name}` `` clean to the same string.
- **Limit:** Like the existing `"..."` and `'...'` handling, this works one line at a time. A template literal that spans several lines isn't normalized. Replacing it across lines would shift the line indexes used for reporting.

Nothing is committed.
